title.zh: 卷四十一 蜀書十一 霍王向張楊費傳
title.en: Volume 41: Book of Shu 11 - Biographies of Huo, Wang, Xiang, Zhang, Yang, and Fei
title.raw: 卷四十一 蜀書十一 霍王向張楊費傳 Volume 41: Book of Shu 11 - Biographies of Huo, Wang, Xiang, Zhang, Yang, and Fei

sentences.zh: 霍峻字仲邈，南郡枝江人也。

translations.literal: Huo Jun, courtesy name Zhongmiao, was a man of Zhijiang in Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Jun, whose courtesy name was Zhongmiao, came from Zhijiang in Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 兄篤於鄉里合部曲數百人，篤卒，荊州牧劉表令峻攝其眾。

translations.literal: His elder brother Huo Du in the home district assembled several hundred retainers as a private host. When Du died, the Inspector of Jing Province, Liu Biao, ordered Jun to take command of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: His older brother Huo Du had raised a private following of several hundred men in their native place. After Du died, Liu Biao, as shepherd of Jing Province, put Jun in charge of that force.

sentences.zh: 表卒，峻率眾歸先主，先主以峻為中郎將。

translations.literal: When Bao died, Jun led his followers to submit to the First Lord; the First Lord appointed him a middle-ranking general.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Biao died, Jun brought his men over to the First Lord, who made him a middle-ranking general.

sentences.zh: 先主自葭萌南還襲劉璋，留峻守葭萌城。

translations.literal: When the First Lord returned south from Jiameng to strike Liu Zhang, he left Jun to defend Jiameng city.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord marched south from Jiameng to surprise Liu Zhang and left Jun to hold Jiameng.

sentences.zh: 張魯遣將楊帛誘峻，求共守城，峻曰：「小人頭可得，城不可得。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu sent his officer Yang Bo to entice Jun, asking to defend the city together. Jun said, "This low man's head may be taken; the city may not."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu sent his general Yang Bo to win Jun over with an offer to hold the city jointly. Jun replied, "You may have my head, but you will not have the city."

sentences.zh: 」帛乃退去。

translations.literal: Bo then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bo withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後璋將扶禁、向存等帥萬餘人由閬水上，攻圍攻峻，且一年，不能下。

translations.literal: Later Zhang's generals Fu Jin, Xiang Cun, and others led more than ten thousand men up the Lang River, besieged and attacked Jun, for nearly a year, and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Zhang's generals Fu Jin and Xiang Cun led over ten thousand men up the Lang River to lay siege to Jun; the siege lasted the better part of a year without success.

sentences.zh: 峻城中兵才數百人，伺其怠隙，選精銳出擊，大破之，即斬存首。

translations.literal: Jun had only several hundred men in the city; watching for their slackness, he chose crack troops, sallied out, routed them greatly, and beheaded Cun.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had only a few hundred defenders. He waited for a gap in their vigilance, picked his best troops for a sortie, shattered their army, and took Xiang Cun's head.

sentences.zh: 先主定蜀，嘉峻之功，乃分廣漢為梓潼郡，以峻為梓潼太守、裨將軍。

translations.literal: After the First Lord pacified Shu, in praise of Jun's merit he carved Guanghan to establish Zitong commandery and appointed Jun administrator of Zitong and a general of the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Once the First Lord had settled Shu, he singled out Jun's achievement, split off Zitong from Guanghan as a new commandery, and named Jun its administrator and a general of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 在官三年，年四十卒，還葬成都。

translations.literal: In office three years, at age forty he died; he was escorted back for burial at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He served three years in office and died at forty; his body was brought back to Chengdu for burial.

sentences.zh: 先主甚悼惜，乃詔諸葛亮曰：「峻既佳士，加有功於國，欲行爵。

translations.literal: The First Lord deeply mourned him and issued an edict to Zhuge Liang saying, "Jun was a fine man who moreover had merit for the state; I wish to carry out enfeoffment."
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord grieved deeply and told Zhuge Liang, "Jun was an excellent man who also served the realm with distinction; I intend to grant him a noble rank."

sentences.zh: 」遂親率群僚臨會弔祭，因留宿墓上，當時榮之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he personally led the assembled officials to the joint mourning sacrifice and lodged overnight on the tomb; at the time it was counted glorious.
translations.idiomatic: He then led the full court to the funeral rites himself and spent the night by the grave—a mark of honor people still spoke of.

sentences.zh: 子 霍弋

translations.literal: Son: Huo Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His son: Huo Yi.

sentences.zh: 子弋，字紹先，行主末年為太子舍人。

translations.literal: The son Yi, courtesy name Shaoxian, in the last years of the First Lord's reign served as attendant to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huo Yi, courtesy name Shaoxian, became an attendant to the heir apparent in the closing years of the First Lord's reign.

sentences.zh: 後主踐阼，除謁者。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord ascended the throne he was appointed usher.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord took the throne, Yi was appointed usher at court.

sentences.zh: 丞相諸葛亮北駐漢中，請為記室，使與子喬共周旋游處。

translations.literal: When the Chancellor Zhuge Liang encamped north at Hanzhong, he requested Yi as secretary on his staff and ordered him to keep company and lodge with his son Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: While Chancellor Zhuge Liang was stationed north at Hanzhong, he asked Yi to serve as his secretary and had him live and travel with Liang's son Zhuge Qiao.

sentences.zh: 亮卒，為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: After Liang died he became a gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang's death he was promoted to gentleman at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 後主立太子璿，以弋為中庶子，璿好騎射，出入無度，弋援引古義，盡言規諫，甚得切磋之體。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord established the heir apparent Xuan, he made Yi junior tutor to the heir; Xuan loved riding and shooting and came and went without restraint, but Yi cited classical precedents and admonished him exhaustively, very much in the manner of mutual polish.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord installed Liu Xuan as heir apparent, he named Yi junior tutor. The heir loved riding and shooting and roamed without limit; Yi cited the classics and remonstrated at length in the best tradition of candid counsel.

sentences.zh: 後為參軍庲降屯副貳都督，又轉護軍，統事如前。

translations.literal: Later he was deputy to the commander of the Lajiang garrison, then shifted to colonel of the guards, with duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as deputy to the commander of the Lajiang garrison, then became colonel of the guards while keeping his former responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 時永昌郡夷獠恃險不賓，數為寇害，乃以弋領永昌太守，率偏軍討之，遂斬其豪帥，破壞邑落，郡界寧靜。

translations.literal: At that time in Yongchang the barbarians of the hills relied on terrain and did not submit, repeatedly raiding as bandits; therefore Yi was given concurrent title as administrator of Yongchang, led a detached force to attack them, beheaded their chieftains, broke their settlements, and the commandery borders were quiet.
translations.idiomatic: The hill peoples of Yongchang had long used the rugged country to defy authority and raid the frontier. Yi was therefore made concurrent administrator of Yongchang, led a detached column against them, executed their headmen, razed their stockades, and restored calm to the commandery.

sentences.zh: 遷監軍、翊軍將軍，領建寧太守，還統南郡事。

translations.literal: He was promoted army supervisor and general who supports the army, with concurrent post as administrator of Jianning, then returned to oversee affairs in Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to army supervisor and general who supports the army, with concurrent appointment as administrator of Jianning, then again took charge of affairs in Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 景耀六年，進號安南將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingyao his title was advanced to general who pacifies the south.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Jingyao era his rank was raised to general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 是歲，蜀並於魏，弋與巴東領軍襄陽羅憲各保全一方，舉以內附，鹹因仍前任，寵待有加。

translations.literal: That year Shu was annexed by Wei; Yi and Luo Xian of Xiangyang, colonel of the guards in Badong, each kept one region secure and offered submission inward; all were allowed to retain their former posts, with favor added.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shu fell to Wei. Yi and Luo Xian of Xiangyang, who commanded the Badong guard, each held his territory intact and then submitted to Wei. They were all allowed to keep their former posts and received still greater marks of favor.

sentences.zh: 〈《汉晋春秋》曰：霍弋闻魏军来，弋欲赴成都，后主以备敌既定，不听。

translations.literal: The Han-Jin Annals says: When Huo Yi heard Wei armies were coming, Yi wished to hurry to Chengdu; the Later Lord, because preparations against the enemy were already settled, would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Han-Jin Annals records that when Huo Yi learned Wei was advancing, he wanted to rush to Chengdu, but the Later Lord, believing the defense was already arranged, refused permission.

sentences.zh: 及成都不守，弋素服号哭，大临三日。

translations.literal: When Chengdu was not held, Yi wore mourning and wailed aloud, observing the grand mourning for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengdu fell, Yi put on mourning, wept openly, and kept the grand mourning for three days.

sentences.zh: 诸将咸劝宜速降，弋曰：“今道路隔塞，未详主之安危，大故去就，不可苟也。

translations.literal: The generals all urged that he should surrender quickly. Yi said, "Now the roads are blocked and cut off; I have not learned in detail whether my lord is safe or in peril. On such a great matter of going or staying one cannot be careless.
translations.idiomatic: His officers all pressed him to yield at once. Yi said, "Communications are cut; I do not yet know whether our sovereign is safe or in danger. A decision of this weight cannot be taken lightly.

sentences.zh: 若主上与魏和，见遇以礼，则保境而降，不晚也。

translations.literal: If my lord makes peace with Wei and is received with ritual courtesy, then to secure the borders and submit would not be late.
translations.idiomatic: If our lord has come to terms with Wei and is treated with proper respect, we can still hold the frontier and surrender then—it would not be too late.

sentences.zh: 若万一危辱，吾将以死拒之，何论迟速邪！

translations.literal: If by any chance he meets danger and disgrace, I will resist with my death— why discuss sooner or later!"
translations.idiomatic: But if he has suffered outrage or ruin, I will meet the invader with my life. What is there to say about haste or delay?"

sentences.zh: ”得后主东迁之问，始率六郡将守上表曰：“臣闻人生於三，事之如一，惟难所在，则致其命。

translations.literal: When he received word the Later Lord had moved east, he then led the generals and defenders of six commanderies in a memorial saying, "I have heard that human life rests on three obligations and serves them as one; wherever difficulty lies, one lays down one's life.
translations.idiomatic: When news arrived that the Later Lord had been moved eastward, he led the officers of six commanderies in a memorial: "I have read that a man owes his life to three bonds and serves them as one; wherever crisis falls, he should give his utmost.

sentences.zh: 今臣国败主附，守死无所，是以委质，不敢有贰。

translations.literal: Now my state is defeated and my lord attached elsewhere; I have no place to die for duty, therefore I present my pledge and dare not harbor two minds."
translations.idiomatic: My country is lost and my sovereign a guest in another court; I have no ground left to die for, so I offer my allegiance and dare not hold a divided heart."

sentences.zh: ”晋文王善之，又拜南中都督，委以本任。

translations.literal: King Wen of Jin praised him; he was also appointed commander of the south center and entrusted with his original charge.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao, king of Jin, approved the memorial and again named Yi commander of the southern interior, leaving him in his former role.

sentences.zh: 后遣将兵救援吕兴，平交阯、日南、九真三郡，功封列侯，进号崇赏焉。

translations.literal: Later he sent troops to rescue Lu Xing, pacified Jiaozhi, Rinan, and Jiuzhen—three commanderies—for merit was enfeoffed a full marquis and his title was advanced with an honorific.
translations.idiomatic: He later dispatched troops to aid Lu Xing, reduced Jiaozhi, Rinan, and Jiuzhen, and for that service was enfeoffed a full marquis with a further honorary generalship.

sentences.zh: 弋孙彪，晋越巂太守。

translations.literal: Yi's grandson Biao was administrator of Yuexi in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Huo Biao became administrator of Yuexi under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 《襄阳记》曰：罗宪字令则。

translations.literal: The Xiangyang Record says: Luo Xian's courtesy name was Lingze.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiangyang Record gives Luo Xian's courtesy name as Lingze.

sentences.zh: 父蒙，避乱於蜀，官至广汉太守。

translations.literal: His father Meng, fleeing turmoil, went to Shu and rose to the rank of administrator of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Luo Meng had fled the wars into Shu and risen to administrator of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 宪少以才学知名，年十三能属文。

translations.literal: Xian was known from youth for talent and learning; at thirteen he could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Xian was known for ability and scholarship; at thirteen he could already write polished essays.

sentences.zh: 后主立太子，为太子舍人，迁庶子、尚书吏部郎，以宣信校尉再使於吴，吴人称美焉。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord established an heir apparent, he served as attendant to the heir, was promoted to junior tutor and director of personnel in the Masters of Writing, and as trust-dispensing colonel twice went on mission to Wu, where men praised him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Later Lord named an heir apparent, Xian served as attendant to the heir, then rose to junior tutor and director of personnel in the Masters of Writing. Twice he went to Wu as trust-dispensing colonel and won admiration there.

sentences.zh: 时黄皓预政，众多附之，宪独不与同，皓恚，左迁巴东太守。

translations.literal: At that time Huang Hao interfered in government; the multitude attached to him; Xian alone did not go along with him; Hao resented him and transferred him left to administrator of Badong.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Hao meddled in state affairs, most officials curried favor with him; Xian alone held aloof. Hao nursed a grudge and had him demoted to administrator of Badong.

sentences.zh: 时右大将军阎宇都督巴东，为领军，后主拜宪为宇副贰。

translations.literal: At that time the great general on the right Yan Yu commanded Badong as army supervisor and was commanding general; the Later Lord appointed Xian as Yan Yu's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The great general on the right, Yan Yu, was army supervisor of Badong and commanding general; the Later Lord made Xian his second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 魏之伐蜀，召宇西还，留宇二千人，令宪守永安城。

translations.literal: When Wei attacked Shu, Yu was summoned west; two thousand of Yu's men were left and Xian was ordered to defend Yongan city.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei invaded Shu, Yan Yu was recalled westward, leaving two thousand men under Xian with orders to hold Yongan.

sentences.zh: 寻闻成都败，城中扰动，江边长吏皆弃城走，宪斩称成都乱者一人，百姓乃定。

translations.literal: Soon he heard Chengdu had been defeated; the city was disturbed; the long officials along the river all abandoned the city and fled; Xian executed one man who claimed Chengdu was in disorder, and the hundred surnames then were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Word soon came that Chengdu had fallen; the town panicked, and riverfront magistrates bolted. Xian executed one man who spread false tales of chaos in the capital, and the populace steadied.

sentences.zh: 得后主委质问至，乃帅所统临于都亭三日。

translations.literal: When he obtained the Later Lord's letter of entrustment and inquiry that arrived, he then led those he commanded to mourn at the assembly pavilion for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord's letter of explanation reached him, he led his command to the roadside pavilion and mourned for three days.

sentences.zh: 吴闻蜀败，起兵西上，外讬救援，内欲袭宪。

translations.literal: Wu heard Shu had been defeated and raised troops westward, outwardly claiming relief but inwardly intending to strike Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Wu learned of Shu's collapse and marched west, claiming to help while actually planning to seize Xian.

sentences.zh: 宪曰：“本朝倾覆，吴为脣齿，不恤我难而徼其利，背盟违约。

translations.literal: Xian said, "Our dynasty has overturned; Wu is lip to our tooth; they do not pity our difficulty but seek our profit— betraying alliance and breaking covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Xian declared, "Our court has fallen. Wu ought to stand with us as lip to tooth, yet instead of pitying our plight they angle for gain— they have broken faith and cast aside the treaty.

sentences.zh: 且汉已亡，吴何得久，宁能为吴降虏乎！

translations.literal: Moreover Han is already gone; how can Wu long endure— could I become one who surrenders a captive to Wu!"
translations.idiomatic: Han is gone; how long can Wu last? Am I to become a prisoner who bends the knee to Wu?"

sentences.zh: ”保城缮甲，告誓将士，厉以节义，莫不用命。

translations.literal: He secured the city, repaired armor, proclaimed oath to officers and men, and roused them with integrity and duty; none failed to obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: He locked the gates, refitted the armor, swore the garrison in, and appealed to duty and honor until every man stood ready.

sentences.zh: 吴闻锺、邓败，百城无主，有兼蜀之志，而巴东固守，兵不得过，使步协率众而西。

translations.literal: Wu heard Zhong and Deng had been defeated and a hundred cities lacked masters, and had the ambition to annex Shu, but Badong held firm and troops could not pass, so Bu Xie led a host westward.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu heard that Zhong Hui and Deng Ai had destroyed each other and a hundred towns were leaderless, it coveted Shu for itself. Badong blocked the route, so Wu sent Bu Xie west with a large force.

sentences.zh: 宪临江拒射，不能御，遣参军杨宗突围北出，告急安东将军陈骞，又送文武印绶、任子诣晋王。

translations.literal: Xian defended along the river with archery and could not withstand them; he sent his aide-de-camp Yang Zong to break out north and report urgent distress to Chen Qian, general who secures the east, and also sent civil and military seals and a hostage son to the king of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Xian tried to hold the line with bowshot but could not stem the tide. He sent his aide Yang Zong to break through northward and beg relief from Chen Qian, general who secures the east, and forwarded his seals of office and a son as hostage to the king of Jin.

sentences.zh: 协攻城，宪出与战，大破其军。

translations.literal: Xie assaulted the city; Xian went out and fought, greatly breaking his army.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xie stormed the walls; Xian sallied forth and shattered his army.

sentences.zh: 孙休怒，复遣陆抗等帅众三万人增宪之围。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu grew angry and again sent Lu Kang and others to lead a host of thirty thousand men to increase the siege of Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu flew into a rage and dispatched Lu Kang and others with thirty thousand men to tighten the siege around Xian.

sentences.zh: 被攻凡六月日而救援不到，城中疾病大半。

translations.literal: He was attacked in all for six months and days and relief did not arrive; in the city more than half fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: The siege ran half a year without relief, and disease carried off more than half the defenders.

sentences.zh: 或说宪奔走之计，宪曰：“夫为人主，百姓所仰，危不能安，急而弃之，君子不为也，毕命於此矣。

translations.literal: Someone urged a plan of flight for Xian; Xian said, "One who is lord of men is what the hundred surnames rely upon— in danger he does not bring peace, in urgency he abandons them: the gentleman does not do this; I will end my life here."
translations.idiomatic: Some counseled retreat. Xian answered, "A leader is what the people lean on. To flee danger and abandon them in crisis is not what a gentleman does. I will die here."

sentences.zh: ”陈骞言於晋王，遣荆州刺史胡烈救宪，抗等引退。

translations.literal: Chen Qian spoke to the king of Jin, who sent Hu Lie, inspector of Jing Province, to rescue Xian; Kang and the rest led away.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qian pleaded with the king of Jin, who sent Hu Lie, inspector of Jing Province, to relieve the city; Lu Kang and his colleagues withdrew.

sentences.zh: 晋王即委前任，拜宪凌江将军，封万年亭侯。

translations.literal: The king of Jin immediately confirmed his former post, appointed Xian general who crosses the river, and enfeoffed him marquis of Wannian village.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Jin at once confirmed his old appointment, named him general who crosses the river, and enfeoffed him as marquis of Wannian village.

sentences.zh: 会武陵四县举众叛吴，以宪为武陵太守巴东监军。

translations.literal: When the four counties of Wuling raised a host in revolt against Wu, Xian was made administrator of Wuling and army supervisor of Badong.
translations.idiomatic: When four counties in Wuling rose against Wu, Xian was appointed administrator of Wuling and army supervisor of Badong.

sentences.zh: 泰始元年改封西鄂县侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taishi his fief was changed to marquis of Xie county.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taishi his fief was moved to marquis of Xie county.

sentences.zh: 宪遣妻子居洛阳，武帝以子袭为给事中。

translations.literal: Xian sent wife and children to dwell in Luoyang; Emperor Wu appointed his son Xi gentleman-in-attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his family to live in Luoyang; Emperor Wu named his son Luo Xi gentleman-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，入朝，进位冠军将军、假节。

translations.literal: In the third year, winter, he entered court and was advanced in rank to general-champion with credential.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taishi, winter, he attended court and was promoted to general-champion with credential.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，从帝宴于华林园，诏问蜀大臣子弟，后问先辈宜时叙用者，宪荐蜀郡常忌、杜轸、寿良、巴西陈寿、南郡高轨、南阳吕雅、许国、江夏费恭、琅邪诸葛京、汝南陈裕，即皆叙用，咸显於世。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year he followed the emperor in a banquet at Hualin Garden; an edict asked about sons and brothers of Shu ministers, then asked about men of earlier generations fit for timely appointment; Xian recommended Chang Ji of Shu commandery, Du Zhen, Shou Liang, Chen Shou of Ba, Gao Gui of Nan commandery, Lu Ya, Xu Guo, Fei Gong of Jiangxia, Zhuge Jing of Langye, Chen Yu of Runan; immediately all were appointed and used, each illustrious in the age.
translations.idiomatic: At a spring banquet in Hualin Park in the fourth year, the emperor asked after the sons and brothers of Shu officials, then who among the older generation deserved prompt employment. Xian nominated Chang Ji, Du Zhen, and Shou Liang of Shu, Chen Shou of Ba, Gao Gui of Nan, Lu Ya, Xu Guo, Fei Gong of Jiangxia, Zhuge Jing of Langye, and Chen Yu of Runan. They were all given posts at once and rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 宪还，袭取吴之巫城，因上伐吴之策。

translations.literal: When Xian returned, he struck and took Wu's city of Wu and thereupon presented a strategy to attack Wu.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he seized Wu's border town of Wu and submitted a plan for conquering Wu.

sentences.zh: 宪方亮严正，待士不倦，轻财好施，不治产业。

translations.literal: Xian was square, bright, and stern, tireless in treating gentlemen, light with wealth and fond of giving, and did not manage estates.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was upright, capable, and strict, never weary of looking after his men, generous with money yet indifferent to personal property.

sentences.zh: 六年薨，赠安南将军，谥曰烈侯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died; he was posthumously honored general who pacifies the south, with posthumous title marquis Exemplary.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Taishi and was posthumously titled general who pacifies the south with the posthumous epithet Lie (Ardent) and a marquis rank.

sentences.zh: 子袭，以凌江将军领部曲，早卒，追赠广汉太守。

translations.literal: His son Xi, as general who crosses the river leading retainers, died early; he was posthumously enfeoffed administrator of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luo Xi, general who crosses the river in command of household troops, died young and was posthumously honored as administrator of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 袭子徽，顺阳内史，永嘉五年为王如所杀。

translations.literal: Xi's son Hui was interior chief of Shunyang; in the fifth year of Yongjia he was killed by Wang Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's son Luo Hui served as interior chief of Shunyang and was killed by the bandit Wang Ru in the fifth year of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 此作“献”，名与本传不同，未详孰是也。〉

translations.literal: Here it writes "present" (xian)— the name differs from this biography; it is not detailed which is correct.
translations.idiomatic: The text here reads "present" for the name, which disagrees with this biography; it is unclear which form is right.

sentences.zh: 王連字文儀，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Lian, courtesy name Wenyi, was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lian, courtesy name Wenyi, was a native of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 劉璋時入蜀為梓潼令。

translations.literal: In Liu Zhang's time he entered Shu and became magistrate of Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Zhang he had crossed into Shu and served as magistrate of Zitong.

sentences.zh: 先主起事葭萌，進軍來南，連閉城不降，先主義之，不強逼也。

translations.literal: When the First Lord raised troops at Jiameng and advanced the army south, Lian closed the city and would not submit; the First Lord deemed him righteous and did not force him.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Lord rose at Jiameng and marched south, Lian barred the gates and refused to yield. The First Lord respected his integrity and did not press the siege.

sentences.zh: 及成都既平，以連為什邡令，轉在廣都，所居有績。

translations.literal: When Chengdu was already pacified, Lian was made magistrate of Shifang, then transferred to Guangdu; where he dwelt there was achievement.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengdu fell he was appointed magistrate of Shifang, then transferred to Guangdu, and in every post he left a record of good government.

sentences.zh: 遷司鹽校尉，較鹽鐵之利，利入甚多，有裨國用，於是簡取良才以為官屬，若呂乂、杜祺、劉干，終皆至大官，自連所拔也。

translations.literal: He was promoted colonel director of the salt [monopoly], compared the profits of salt and iron, and revenue entered in great amount, benefiting state use; therefore he selected able men for office staff, such as Lu Yi, Du Qi, and Liu Gan, who in the end all reached high office— from Lian's promotions.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to colonel director of the salt and iron monopolies, reorganized their revenues, and greatly increased the income that fed the treasury. He picked able men for his staff— Lu Yi, Du Qi, Liu Gan among them— who all rose to high rank on his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 遷蜀郡太守、興業將軍，領鹽府如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted administrator of Shu commandery and general who establishes enterprise, continuing to head the salt office as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to administrator of Shu commandery and general who establishes enterprise while still overseeing the salt administration.

sentences.zh: 建興元年，拜屯騎校尉，領丞相長史，封平陽亭侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianxing he was appointed colonel of the agile cavalry, concurrent chief clerk to the chancellor, and enfeoffed marquis of Pingyang village.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianxing he became colonel of the agile cavalry and chief clerk to the chancellor, with a marquisate at Pingyang village.

sentences.zh: 時南方諸郡不賓，諸葛亮將自征之，連諫以為「此不毛之地，疫癘之鄉，不宜以一國之望，冒險而行」。

translations.literal: At that time the southern commanderies did not submit; Zhuge Liang would personally campaign against them; Lian remonstrated, deeming that "this is land that bears no crops, a country of pestilence; it is not fitting that the hope of a whole state should risk danger and go."
translations.idiomatic: The southern commanderies were still in revolt, and Zhuge Liang meant to lead the expedition himself. Lian urged against it: "That country is barren malarial ground; the fate of the realm should not be wagered on such a march."

sentences.zh: 亮慮諸將才不及己，意欲必往而連言輒懇至，故停留者久之。

translations.literal: Liang worried that the generals' talent did not match his own and inwardly wished certainly to go, while Lian's words were repeatedly earnest; therefore he halted for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Liang doubted any general could match his own ability and was determined to go, yet Lian's pleas were so urgent that the campaign was postponed for a long while.

sentences.zh: 會連卒。

translations.literal: It happened that Lian died.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wang Lian died.

sentences.zh: 子山嗣，官至江陽太守。

translations.literal: The son Shan inherited; in office he reached administrator of Jiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Shan succeeded him and rose to administrator of Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 向朗字巨達，襄陽宜城人也。

translations.literal: Xiang Lang, courtesy name Jufa, was a man of Yicheng in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Lang, courtesy name Jufa, came from Yicheng in Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 〈《襄阳记》曰：朗少师事司马德操，与徐元直、韩德高、庞士元皆亲善。〉

translations.literal: The Xiangyang Record says: In youth Lang studied under Sima Decao and was intimate with Xu Yuanzhi, Han Degao, and Pang Shiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiangyang Record notes that in youth he studied under Sima Hui and was close to Xu Shu, Han Song, and Pang Tong.

sentences.zh: 荊州牧劉表以為臨沮長。

translations.literal: The shepherd of Jing Province, Liu Biao, appointed him magistrate of Linju.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao, as shepherd of Jing Province, made him magistrate of Linju.

sentences.zh: 表卒，歸先主。

translations.literal: When Bao died, he returned to the First Lord.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Biao died he joined the First Lord.

sentences.zh: 先主定江南，使朗督秭歸、夷道、巫

translations.literal: When the First Lord pacified the south of the river, he had Lang supervise Zigui, Yidao, Wu
translations.idiomatic: After the First Lord secured the south bank of the Yangzi, he put Lang in overall charge of Zigui, Yidao, and Wu

translations.literal: (mountain)
translations.idiomatic: (the text inserts the character “mountain,” yielding “Wushan”)

sentences.zh: 、夷陵四縣軍民事。

translations.literal: and Yiling—four counties.
translations.idiomatic: and Yiling—four counties in all, with charge of their military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 蜀既平，以朗為巴西太守，頃之轉任，又徙房陵。

translations.literal: When Shu was already pacified, Lang was made administrator of Ba commandery; shortly he was transferred in office, then moved to Fangling.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shu was pacified he became administrator of Ba, served briefly elsewhere, and was then posted to Fangling.

sentences.zh: 后主践阼，为步兵校尉，代王连领丞相长史。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord ascended the throne, he became colonel of the footmen, replacing Wang Lian as chief clerk to the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord took the throne, Lang was made colonel of the footmen and succeeded Wang Lian as chief clerk to the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮南征，朗留统后事。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Liang campaigned south, Lang stayed to oversee rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While Chancellor Liang marched south, Lang remained behind to manage the rear administration.

sentences.zh: 五年，隨亮漢中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Liang to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jianxing he accompanied Liang to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 朗素與馬謖善，謖逃亡，朗知情不舉，亮恨之，免官還成都。

translations.literal: Lang had long been on good terms with Ma Su; when Su fled, Lang knew but did not report; Liang resented him, stripped his office, and sent him back to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Lang had long been friendly with Ma Su; when Su deserted after his defeat, Lang knew but said nothing. Liang was furious, dismissed him, and sent him home to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 數年，為光祿勳，亮卒後徒左將軍，追論舊功，封顯明亭侯，位特進。

translations.literal: After several years he was minister of the household; after Liang died he was transferred to general of the left; tracing old merit he was enfeoffed marquis of the Xianming village at special advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he became minister of the household, and after Liang's death was shifted to general of the left. His earlier service was remembered and he was enfeoffed marquis of the Xianming village with the rank of special advancement.

sentences.zh: 初，朗少時雖涉獵文學，然不治素檢，以吏能稱。

translations.literal: In the beginning, in youth Lang had read widely in letters, yet did not regulate himself by plain conduct; he was praised for administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he had read widely but cared little for conventional restraint; people valued him chiefly as an administrator.

sentences.zh: 自去長史，優遊無事垂三十年，

translations.literal: From leaving the chief clerk post, leisurely without affairs, nearly thirty years,
translations.idiomatic: After losing the chief clerkship he lived at ease for almost thirty years,

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：朗坐马谡免长史，则建兴六年中也。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates: Lang sat for Ma Su and was dismissed as chief clerk, then it was the sixth year of Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks: Lang lost the chief clerk's post over Ma Su in the sixth year of Jianxing.

sentences.zh: 朗至延熙十年卒，整二十年耳，此云“三十”，字之误也。〉

translations.literal: Lang died in the tenth year of Yanxi— a full twenty years; here saying "thirty" is an error in the character.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Yanxi— only twenty years later— so the "thirty" here is a scribal mistake.

sentences.zh: 乃更潛心典籍，孜孜不倦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he turned his mind more deeply to the classical collections without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He then buried himself in the classics with tireless devotion.

sentences.zh: 年逾八十，猶手自校書，刊定謬誤，積聚篇卷，於時最多。

translations.literal: Past eighty he still personally collated books, corrected errors, and accumulated fascicles; of the time he had the most.
translations.idiomatic: Past eighty he still collated texts with his own hand, emending mistakes, and amassed more rolls than anyone of his day.

sentences.zh: 開門接賓，誘納後進，但講論古義，不干時事，以是見稱。

translations.literal: He opened the gate to receive guests and guided younger entrants, but only lectured on ancient meanings and did not touch current affairs; for this he was praised.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed students and nurtured the young, confining his teaching to antiquity and never meddling in politics— for which he was widely admired.

sentences.zh: 上自執政，下及童冠，皆敬重焉。

translations.literal: From those who held power down to youths in caps all respected him.
translations.idiomatic: From high ministers down to lads in scholars' caps, everyone held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 延熙十年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the tenth year of Yanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Yanxi.

sentences.zh: 〈襄阳记曰：朗遗言戒子曰：“传称师克在和不在众，此言天地和则万物生，君臣和则国家平，九族和则动得所求，静得所安，是以圣人守和，以存以亡也。

translations.literal: The Xiangyang Record says: Lang's dying words admonishing his sons said, "The tradition says the army prevails in harmony, not in numbers," this saying means when heaven and earth are harmonious the myriad things are born; when ruler and minister are harmonious the state is level; when the nine branches of kin are harmonious, in motion one obtains what is sought, in stillness one obtains peace; therefore the sage guards harmony in order to preserve or perish.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiangyang Record preserves his deathbed advice to his sons: "The canon says victory lies in unity, not in numbers. When heaven and earth are at peace the myriad things thrive; when lord and subject are at peace the realm is steady; when the wider family is at peace, you find what you seek in action and rest in repose. That is why the sage cherishes harmony as the root of survival or ruin.

sentences.zh: 吾，楚国之小子耳，而早丧所天，为二兄所诱养，使其性行不随禄利以堕。

translations.literal: I am but a lad of Chu who early lost what heaven gave me and was led on to be reared by two elder brothers, causing my nature and conduct not to follow salary and profit to sink.
translations.idiomatic: I am only a boy from Chu who lost his father too soon and was raised by two older brothers who guided me, so that my character never slid into greed for rank and gain.

sentences.zh: 今但贫耳；

translations.literal: Now I am only poor;
translations.idiomatic: Today I have nothing but poverty;

sentences.zh: 贫非人患，惟和为贵，汝其勉之！

translations.literal: poverty is not a human calamity; only harmony is precious— you must strive for it!
translations.idiomatic: poverty itself is no disaster; harmony is what counts— strive for that above all!

translations.literal: The quoted admonition ends and the excerpt from the Xiangyang Record closes here.
translations.idiomatic: Here the quotation and the annotation block come to a close.

sentences.zh: 子條嗣，景耀中為御史中丞。

translations.literal: The son Tiao inherited; in the Jingyao era he was palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang Tiao succeeded him and, during the Jingyao years, became palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 〈襄阳记曰：条字文豹，亦博学多识，入晋为江阳太守、南中军司马。〉

translations.literal: The Xiangyang Record states: Tiao's courtesy name was Wenbao; he too was learned and well informed; entering the Jin he became administrator of Jiangyang and army marshal of the southern interior.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiangyang Record adds that Tiao's courtesy name was Wenbao, that he was as erudite as his father, and that under the Jin he rose to administrator of Jiangyang and army marshal of the southern interior.

sentences.zh: 侄 向寵

translations.literal: Nephew: Xiang Chong.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew: Xiang Chong.

sentences.zh: 張裔字君嗣，蜀郡成都人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Junsu, was a man of Chengdu in Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Junsu, came from Chengdu in Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 治《公羊春秋》，博涉《史》、《漢》。

translations.literal: He studied 《the Gongyang commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals》 and read widely in 《the Records of the Historian》 and 《the Book of Han》.
translations.idiomatic: He specialized in 《the Gongyang commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals》 and ranged widely through 《the Records of the Historian》 and 《the Book of Han》.

sentences.zh: 汝南許文休入蜀，謂裔干裡敏捷，是中夏鐘元常之倫也。

translations.literal: When Xu Wenxiu of Runan entered Shu, he said Yi was keen and quick-witted over a thousand li and was of the same class as Zhong Yuanchang of the central plain.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Shao of Runan came into Shu, he pronounced Yi as sharp and resourceful as anyone within a thousand li— the equal of Zhong Yao of the heartland.

sentences.zh: 劉璋時，舉孝廉，為魚復長，還州署從事，領帳下司馬。

translations.literal: In Liu Zhang's time he was recommended as filial and incorrupt, became magistrate of Yufu, returned to the province as an adjutant, and concurrently led headquarters marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Zhang he earned recommendation as filial and incorrupt, served as magistrate of Yufu, then came back to headquarters as an adjutant commanding the marshal of the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 張飛自荊州由墊江入，璋授裔兵，拒張飛於德陽陌下，軍敗，還成都。

translations.literal: Zhang Fei came from Jing Province through Dianjiang; Zhang gave Yi troops to resist Zhang Fei below the Deyang mo; the army was defeated and returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei advanced from Jing Province via Dianjiang. Liu Zhang armed Yi and sent him to block Zhang Fei on the Deyang plain; Yi's force was routed and he fell back to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 為璋奉使詣先主，先主許以禮其君而安其人也，裔還，城門乃開。

translations.literal: He was sent by Zhang on mission to the First Lord; the First Lord promised with ritual to treat his lord and settle the people; Yi returned and then the city gates were opened.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang then dispatched Yi as envoy to the First Lord, who pledged to honor Liu Zhang by rite and to spare the people. Yi brought back that promise, and only then did the gates open.

sentences.zh: 先主以裔巴郡太守，還為司金中郎將，典作農戰之器。

translations.literal: The First Lord appointed Yi administrator of Ba commandery, then returned him to be colonel director of metals, in charge of making implements for farming and war.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord named Yi administrator of Ba, then recalled him to the post of colonel director of metals, responsible for forging tools for both tillage and campaigning.

sentences.zh: 先是，益州郡殺太守正昂，耆率雍闓恩信著於南土，使命周旋，遠通孫權。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Yi Province commandery they had killed the administrator Zheng Ang; the elder leader Yong Kai's favor and trust were renowned in the south, and envoys went back and forth, opening distant communication with Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the people of Yi Province commandery had slain their prefect Zheng Ang. Yong Kai, a headman whose word carried weight in the south, shuttled envoys and even opened contact with Sun Quan far to the east.

sentences.zh: 乃以裔為益州太守，逕往至郡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yi was made administrator of Yi Province commandery and went straight to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was therefore appointed prefect of Yi Province commandery and set out at once for his seat.

sentences.zh: 闓遂趑趄不賓，假鬼教曰：「張府君如瓠壺，外雖澤而內實粗，不足殺，令縛與吳。

translations.literal: Kai then hesitated and would not submit; feigning a ghost's teaching he said, "Administrator Zhang is like a gourd bottle— outside glossy but inside truly coarse; not worth killing— bind him and give him to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Kai stalled and refused allegiance. Posing a spirit oracle he said, "Prefect Zhang is like a lacquered gourd— smooth on the outside but hollow and rough within. He is not worth killing; tie him up and hand him over to Wu.

sentences.zh: 」於是遂送裔於權。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon they sent Yi to Quan.
translations.idiomatic: They did exactly that and shipped Yi off to Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 會先主薨，諸葛亮遣鄧芝使吳，亮令芝言次可從權請裔。

translations.literal: It happened the First Lord died; Zhuge Liang sent Deng Zhi on mission to Wu, and Liang ordered Zhi in the course of conversation to ask Quan for Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Lord died, Zhuge Liang sent Deng Zhi to Wu and told him to work into the talks a request that Sun Quan return Zhang Yi.

sentences.zh: 裔自至吳數年，流徒伏匿，權未之知也，故許芝遣裔。

translations.literal: From the time Yi arrived in Wu for several years, drifting in exile and hiding in concealment, Quan had not known of him, therefore permitted Zhi to send Yi away.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had spent years in Wu as a fugitive in hiding, so Sun Quan had lost track of him and readily agreed to let Deng Zhi take him back.

sentences.zh: 裔臨發，權乃引見。

translations.literal: When Yi was about to depart, Quan then led him in to an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Only as Yi was boarding to leave did Sun Quan summon him for a formal audience.

sentences.zh: 問裔曰：「蜀卓氏寡女，亡奔司馬相如，貴土風俗何以乃爾乎？

translations.literal: He asked Yi saying, "The widowed daughter of the Zhuo clan of Shu ran away to join Sima Xiangru— how can the customs of your noble land be thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan asked, "The Zhuo widow of Shu eloped with Sima Xiangru— is that really how things are done in your country?"

sentences.zh: 」裔對曰：「愚以為卓氏之寡女，猶賢於買臣之妻。

translations.literal: 」Yi replied saying, "I foolishly think the Zhuo clan's widowed daughter was still worthier than the wife of Mai Chen."
translations.idiomatic: Yi answered, "I would say the Zhuo widow still showed more sense than Zhu Maichen's wife."

sentences.zh: 」權又謂裔曰：「君還，必用事西朝，終不作田父子閭裡也，將何以報我？

translations.literal: 」Quan again said to Yi, "When you return, you will surely hold office in the western court and in the end will not be a father and son plowing in the lanes— how will you repay me?"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan pressed him: "Back in Shu you will rise high in the western court; you will not end your days as a peasant in the lanes. What return do you intend for me?"

sentences.zh: 」裔對曰：「裔負罪而歸，將委命有司。

translations.literal: 」Yi replied saying, "Yi returns bearing guilt and will entrust his fate to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "I go home a guilty man and leave my life in the hands of the law.

sentences.zh: 若蒙僥倖得全首領，五十八已前父母之年也，自此已後大王之賜也。

translations.literal: If by luck I keep my head, before fifty-eight that is the span of my parents' years; after this what the great king grants."
translations.idiomatic: If I am spared execution, anything before my fifty-eighth year belongs to my parents' allotted span; whatever comes after is a gift from Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」權言笑歡悅，有器裔之色。

translations.literal: 」Quan spoke and laughed with pleasure, with a bearing that valued Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan laughed and chatted happily, plainly impressed by him.

sentences.zh: 裔出閣，深悔不能陽愚，即便就船，倍道兼行。

translations.literal: When Yi left the gate, he deeply regretted that he could not have played the fool; immediately he boarded the boat and doubled the road, marching day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Once outside the palace Yi cursed himself for not feigning stupidity; he leapt aboard and raced homeward by forced marches.

sentences.zh: 權果追之，裔已入永安界數十里，追者不能及。

translations.literal: Quan indeed pursued him; Yi had already entered Yongan territory several tens of li and the pursuers could not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan did send riders in pursuit, but Yi was already dozens of li inside the Yongan frontier and the pursuers could not overtake him.

sentences.zh: 既至蜀，丞相亮以為參軍，署府事，又領益州治中從事。

translations.literal: After reaching Shu, Chancellor Liang made him an army adviser, assigned him bureau affairs, and also gave him concurrent post as adjutant for the administration of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Shu the chancellor made him an army adviser, put him in charge of headquarters business, and added the title of adjutant for Yi Province administration.

sentences.zh: 亮出駐漢中，裔以射聲校尉領留府長史，常稱曰：「公賞不遺遠，罰不阿近，爵不可以無功取，刑不可以貴勢免，此賢愚之所以僉忘其身者也。

translations.literal: When Liang went out to garrison Hanzhong, Yi as colonel of the sound-shooters led chief clerk to the rear headquarters; he often declared saying, "The duke in rewards does not omit the distant, in punishments does not favor the near; noble rank cannot be taken without merit, punishment cannot be escaped by noble power— this is why worthy and foolish alike forget their persons."
translations.idiomatic: When Liang marched to Hanzhong, Yi stayed behind as colonel of the sound-shooters and chief clerk of the rear headquarters. He used to say, "The duke rewards the far-off and does not spare the mighty in punishment; no one wins a fief without merit, and rank cannot buy exemption from the law— that is why both wise and simple give him their lives."

sentences.zh: 」其明年，北詣亮諮事，送者數百，車乘盈路，裔還書與所親曰：「近者涉道，晝夜接客，不得寧息，人自敬丞相長史，男子張君嗣附之，疲倦欲死。

translations.literal: 」The next year he went north to consult Liang on affairs; several hundred saw him off and carriages filled the road; Yi returned a letter to those close saying, "Recently I traveled the road, day and night receiving guests without obtaining peaceful rest; people themselves revere the chief clerk to the chancellor— the man Zhang Junsu attached to it, weary to the point of wishing to die.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he rode north to consult Liang; hundreds came to see him off and the road was jammed with carts. He wrote home to friends, "I have just been on the road entertaining callers day and night without a moment's rest. They do not honor Zhang Yi; they honor the chief clerk to the chancellor. Being mistaken for that man is exhausting enough to kill you."

sentences.zh: 」其談啁流速，皆此類也。

translations.literal: 」His jesting banter and fluent speed were all of this class.
translations.idiomatic: His quick wit and teasing talk were all in this vein.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以为谈啁贵於机捷，书疏可容留意。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that banter values quickness of wit, whereas a letter may take care.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi comments that repartee lives by sharpness, while a written note may afford more polish.

sentences.zh: 今因书疏之巧，以著谈啁之速，非其理也。〉

translations.literal: To borrow the polish of a written note in order to display the speed of repartee is not sound method.
translations.idiomatic: Using the finish of a formal letter to stand in for the sparkle of live banter is a poor fit.

sentences.zh: 少與犍為楊恭友善，恭早死，遺孤未數歲，裔迎留，與分屋而居，事恭母如母。

translations.literal: In youth he was friendly with Yang Gong of Qianwei; Gong died early, leaving an orphan not yet several years of age; Yi welcomed and kept him, dwelling in a divided house, and served Gong's mother as his own mother.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was close to Yang Gong of Qianwei. When Gong died young, leaving a son still a toddler, Yi took the boy in, gave him a separate wing of the house, and cared for Gong's mother as his own.

sentences.zh: 恭之子息長大，為之娶婦，買田宅產業，使立門戶。

translations.literal: When Gong's sons grew, he for them took wives, bought fields, houses, and property, and enabled them to establish households.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong's children grew up, Yi found them wives, bought farms and houses, and set them up with estates of their own.

sentences.zh: 撫恤故舊，振贍衰宗，行義甚至。

translations.literal: He comforted old friends, aided declining clans, and his conduct of righteousness reached an extreme.
translations.idiomatic: He looked after old companions, supported struggling kinsmen, and carried his sense of duty to rare lengths.

sentences.zh: 加輔漢將軍，領長史如故。

translations.literal: He was advanced general who assists Han, continuing as chief clerk as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who assists Han while retaining his post as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 建興八年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year of Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Jianxing.

sentences.zh: 子毣嗣，

translations.literal: The son Mao inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Mao inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 〈毣音忙角反，见字林，曰“毣，思貌也”。〉

translations.literal: The graph mao is read mang-jue fan; the Zilin gloss says mao denotes a thoughtful mien.
translations.idiomatic: The character mao is given the reading mang-jue in the Zilin, which defines it as a thoughtful expression.

sentences.zh: 歷三郡守、監軍。

translations.literal: He passed through three commandery governorships and army supervision.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of three commanderies and as an army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 毣郁，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Mao's son Yu, junior tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao's son Zhang Yu became junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 楊洪字季休，犍為武陽人也。

translations.literal: Yang Hong, courtesy name Jixiu, was a man of Wuyang in Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hong, courtesy name Jixiu, came from Wuyang in Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 劉璋時歷部諸郡。

translations.literal: In Liu Zhang's time he passed through service in various commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Zhang he had served in several commanderies.

sentences.zh: 先主定蜀，太守李嚴命為功曹。

translations.literal: When the First Lord pacified Shu, the Administrator Li Yan appointed him merit assessor.
translations.idiomatic: After the First Lord conquered Shu, Prefect Li Yan named him merit assessor.

sentences.zh: 嚴欲徒郡治捨，洪固諫不聽，遂辭功曹，請退。

translations.literal: Yan wished to move the commandery seat; Hong firmly remonstrated and was not listened to; therefore he resigned as merit assessor and requested withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan wanted to relocate the prefectural seat. Hong argued fiercely and was ignored, so he resigned as merit assessor and asked to step down.

translations.idiomatic: (wished to)

translations.idiomatic: recommended Hong to the province as

translations.literal: (adjutant for the Shu section)
translations.idiomatic: (the post was adjutant for the Shu section)

sentences.zh: [部蜀從事]。

translations.literal: [adjutant for the Shu section].
translations.idiomatic: [adjutant for the Shu section].

sentences.zh: 先主爭漢中，急書發兵，軍師將軍諸葛亮以問洪，洪曰：「漢中則益州咽喉，存亡之機會，若無漢中則無蜀矣，此家門之禍也。

translations.literal: When the First Lord contested Hanzhong, urgent letters called out troops; the army adviser general Zhuge Liang asked Hong; Hong said, "Hanzhong is the throat of Yi Province, the pivot of survival or destruction; if there is no Hanzhong there is no Shu— this is a calamity at the family gate.
translations.idiomatic: During the struggle for Hanzhong the First Lord sent urgent orders for reinforcements. Zhuge Liang, as army adviser general, asked Hong's view. Hong said, "Hanzhong is Yi Province's windpipe; on it hangs survival. Lose Hanzhong and Shu cannot stand— this is a disaster on our own doorstep.

sentences.zh: 方今之事，男子當戰，女子當運，發兵何疑？

translations.literal: As for the matter now, men should fight and women should transport— why doubt sending troops?"
translations.idiomatic: For this crisis every man should bear arms and every woman should haul supplies— why should we hesitate to mobilize?"

sentences.zh: 」時蜀郡太守法正從先主北行，亮於是表洪領蜀郡太守，眾事皆辦，遂使即真。

translations.literal: 」At that time the Administrator of Shu Fa Zheng accompanied the First Lord north; Liang thereupon memorialized Hong to lead as Administrator of Shu; all affairs were handled, then he was ordered to take substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Fa Zheng, prefect of Shu, had gone north with the First Lord, so Liang memorialized Hong as acting prefect of Shu. Hong cleared every item of business and was soon confirmed in the post.

sentences.zh: 頃之，轉為益州治中從事。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to adjutant for the administration of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was shifted to adjutant for Yi Province administration.

sentences.zh: 五年，丞相亮北住漢中，欲用張裔為留府長史，問洪何如？

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Chancellor Liang north garrisoned Hanzhong and wished to use Zhang Yi as chief clerk to the rear headquarters; he asked Hong how it was?
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jianxing, while Chancellor Liang was stationed north at Hanzhong, he meant to appoint Zhang Yi chief clerk of the rear headquarters and asked Hong what he thought?

sentences.zh: 洪對曰：「裔天姿明察，長於治劇，才誠堪之，然性不公平，恐不可專任，不如留向朗。

translations.literal: Hong replied saying, "Yi's natural endowment is bright and perceptive; he excels at managing acute affairs; his talent truly suffices for it, yet his nature is not fair; I fear he cannot be solely entrusted— better leave Xiang Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong answered, "Zhang Yi is brilliant and sees through detail; he shines at knotty administration and could fill the role, but he is not evenhanded. I would not give him sole charge— better keep Xiang Lang in place.

sentences.zh: 朗情偽差少，裔隨從目下，效其器能，於事兩善。

translations.literal: Lang's true and false differ a little; Yi follows at eye level below, displaying his vessel and ability— on affairs both are good."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Lang is steadier in judgment, while Yi stays close at hand where you can test his capacity— both arrangements serve you well."

sentences.zh: 」初，裔少與洪親善。

translations.literal: 」In the beginning, in youth Yi and Hong were intimate and good.
translations.idiomatic: In their youth Zhang Yi and Yang Hong had been close friends.

sentences.zh: 裔流放在吳，洪臨裔郡，裔子郁給郡吏，微過受罰，不特原假。

translations.literal: Yi was exiled in Wu; when Hong came to Yi's commandery, Yi's son Yu served as a commandery clerk, had a slight fault and received punishment, not specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yi languished in exile in Wu. When Hong became prefect of Yi's old commandery, Yi's son Zhang Yu served as a clerk there; Yu committed a minor offense and Hong punished him without special leniency.

sentences.zh: 裔後還聞之，深以為恨，與洪情好有損。

translations.literal: After Yi later returned and heard it, he deeply took it as resentment, and with Hong affection and friendship had damage.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi eventually came home and learned of it, he nursed a deep grudge, and the bond between him and Hong cooled.

sentences.zh: 及洪見亮出，至裔許，具說所言。

translations.literal: When Hong saw Liang go out, he arrived at Yi's lodging and fully explained what was said.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang set out for the front, Hong visited Yi and repeated word for word what he had told the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 裔答洪曰：「公留我了矣，明府不能止。

translations.literal: Yi answered Hong saying, "The duke has kept me— the enlightened prefect cannot stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Yi told Hong, "The chancellor has already settled on me; our worthy prefect cannot change that.

sentences.zh: 」時人或疑洪意自欲作長史，或疑洪知裔自嫌，不願裔處要職，典後事也。

translations.literal: 」People of the time some suspected Hong's intention was himself to wish to be chief clerk, some suspected Hong knew Yi's self-dislike and did not wish Yi to hold a crucial post managing rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Some thought Hong angled for the chief clerkship himself; others thought he knew Yi resented him and meant to block Yi from a powerful rear post.

sentences.zh: 後裔與司鹽校尉岑述不和，至於忿恨。

translations.literal: Later Yi and the colonel director of the salt Cen Shu were not harmonious, reaching to bitter hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Yi and Cen Shu, the colonel director of the salt monopoly, fell into a feud that turned venomous.

sentences.zh: 亮與裔書曰：「君昔在[陌]下，營壞，吾之用心，食不知味；

translations.literal: Liang wrote a letter to Yi saying, "Sir, once below [the mo], when the camp was ruined, my heart's application— I ate without knowing taste;
translations.idiomatic: Liang wrote to Yi: "When you were trapped below the Deyang plain and your camp was shattered, I was so anxious I could not taste my food;

sentences.zh: 後流洪迸南海，相為悲歎，寢不安席；

translations.literal: later when you were cast adrift toward the southern seas, for each other we lamented sorrowfully and could not sleep peacefully on the mat;
translations.idiomatic: when you were driven off toward the southern seas we mourned for each other and lay awake at night;

sentences.zh: 及其來還，委付大任，同獎王室，自以為與君古之石交也。

translations.literal: when you came back and were entrusted with a great charge, together we aided the royal house— I myself thought with you it was the stone friendship of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: and when you returned to a great trust and we worked together for the house of Han, I believed we shared the kind of bond ancients called a friendship carved in stone.

sentences.zh: 石交之道，舉仇以相益，割骨肉以相明，猶不相謝也，況吾但委意於元儉，而君不能忍邪？

translations.literal: The way of stone friendship raises an enemy to benefit each other, cuts flesh and bone to clarify each other, and still does not decline— how much the more when I only entrusted my mind to Yuanjian, yet you could not endure?"
translations.idiomatic: Such friends recommend even a personal enemy if it helps the other, or cut kin asunder to prove good faith— and still feel no debt. Can you not bear the fact that I merely leaned on Yang Hong for advice?"

sentences.zh: 」論者由是明洪無私。

translations.literal: 」Discussers from this clarified Hong had no selfishness.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers realized then that Hong had acted without private motive.

sentences.zh: 洪少不好學問，而忠清款亮，憂公如家，事繼母至孝。

translations.literal: Hong in youth did not love learning, yet was loyal, pure, sincere, and bright, worrying for the duke as for family, serving his stepmother with extreme filiality.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had never cared much for scholarship, but he was loyal, honest, and transparent, treating public duty as family duty and honoring his stepmother with utmost filial piety.

sentences.zh: 六年卒官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the sixth year of Jianxing.

sentences.zh: 始洪為李嚴功曹，嚴未
