translations.idiomatic: (reached)

sentences.zh: [去]犍為而洪已為蜀郡。

translations.literal: [left] Jianwei when Hong was already administrator of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: [left] Jianwei when Hong was already administrator of Shu.

sentences.zh: 洪迎門下書佐何祗，有才策功干，舉郡吏，數年為廣漢太守，時洪亦尚在蜀郡。

translations.literal: Hong welcomed the clerk under the gate He Zhi, who had talent, stratagem, and meritorious capacity; he recommended him as commandery clerk; in several years he became administrator of Guanghan; at that time Hong also still was in Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had taken on his clerk He Zhi, a man of plans and practical gifts, and raised him to commandery clerk. Within a few years Zhi was prefect of Guanghan while Hong still governed Shu.

sentences.zh: 是以西土鹹服諸葛亮能盡時人之器用也。

translations.literal: Therefore the western lands all submitted that Zhuge Liang could exhaust the vessels and uses of the men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: People across the west agreed that Zhuge Liang knew how to place every man according to his gifts.

sentences.zh: 〈益部耆旧传杂记曰：每朝会，祗次洪坐。

translations.literal: The assorted records of the elders of Yi state: at each court session Zhi sat next to Hong.
translations.idiomatic: The assorted records of the elders of Yi note that at each court session Zhi sat next to Hong.

sentences.zh: 嘲祗曰：“君马何驶？

translations.literal: He mocked Zhi saying, "Why does your horse gallop so fast?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong teased him, "Why is your horse so fast today?"

sentences.zh: ”祗曰：“故吏马不敢驶，但明府未著鞭耳。

translations.literal: 」Zhi said, "A former clerk's horse does not dare gallop fast— only the enlightened prefect has not yet applied the whip."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi shot back, "A former clerk's horse does not dare bolt— unless his lord has not yet raised the crop."

sentences.zh: ”众传之以为笑。

translations.literal: 」The crowd transmitted it and took it as laughter.
translations.idiomatic: The story spread and became a standing joke.

sentences.zh: 祗字君肃，少寒贫，为人宽厚通济，体甚壮大，又能饮食，好声色，不持节俭，故时人少贵之者。

translations.literal: Zhi's courtesy name was Junsu; in youth he was cold and poor, as a person generous and thick and universally helpful, his body very large and strong, and also able to eat and drink, fond of sound and color, not maintaining frugality, therefore men of the time few valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhi, courtesy name Junsu, grew up in bitter poverty yet was openhanded and accommodating. He was a big man with a big appetite and a taste for music and women, careless of thrift, so contemporaries thought little of him.

sentences.zh: 尝梦井中生桑，以问占梦赵直，直曰：“桑非井中之物，会当移植；

translations.literal: He once dreamed a mulberry grew in a well and with it asked the dream-diviner Zhao Zhi; Zhi said, "Mulberry is not a thing of a well— in time it will be transplanted;
translations.idiomatic: He once dreamed mulberries sprouting in a well and asked the diviner Zhao Zhi to interpret it. Zhao said, "Mulberries do not belong in a well; the omen points to a change of post;

sentences.zh: 然桑字四十下八，君寿恐不过此。

translations.literal: yet the character sang is forty below eight— your lifespan I fear will not pass this."
translations.idiomatic: yet the graph for “mulberry” breaks into “forty-eight”— I fear you will not live past forty-eight."

sentences.zh: ”祗笑言“得此足矣”。

translations.literal: 」Zhi laughed saying, "Obtaining this is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi laughed and said, "If I get that far, I shall be content."

sentences.zh: 初仕郡，后为督军从事。

translations.literal: At first he served the commandery, later became supervising army adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: He began in the prefectural office, then became supervising army adjutant.

sentences.zh: 时诸葛亮用法峻密，阴闻祗游戏放纵，不勤所职，尝奄往录狱。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuge Liang used the law sternly and densely; secretly hearing Zhi played and was unrestrained, not diligent in his office, he once suddenly went to record the prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang's justice was strict. Hearing that Zhi idled and caroused instead of tending his duties, Liang once descended on the jail without warning to review the dockets.

sentences.zh: 众人咸为祗惧。

translations.literal: The crowd all for Zhi feared.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone feared for him.

sentences.zh: 祗密闻之，夜张灯火见囚，读诸解状。

translations.literal: Zhi secretly heard it; at night he spread lamps and fire, saw the prisoners, and read all the documents of defense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi got wind of the visit. That night he lit the lamps, went through the cells, and read every plea and defense.

sentences.zh: 诸葛晨往，祗悉已闇诵，答对解释，无所凝滞，亮甚异之。

translations.literal: Zhuge in the morning went; Zhi had already dark-memorized all, answered and explained, without any stagnation; Liang greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang arrived at dawn, Zhi had memorized the files verbatim, answered every question without hesitation, and left Liang astonished.

sentences.zh: 出补成都令，时郫县令缺，以祗兼二县。

translations.literal: He went out to supplement as magistrate of Chengdu; at that time the magistrate of Pi was vacant; with Zhi concurrently holding two counties.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as magistrate of Chengdu while the Pi seat stood empty, so he held both counties at once.

sentences.zh: 二县户口猥多，切近都治，饶诸奸秽，每比人，常眠睡，值其觉寤，辄得奸诈，众咸畏祗之发摘，或以为有术，无敢欺者。

translations.literal: The two counties' household registrations were very numerous, cutting close to the metropolitan administration, rich in various treachery and filth; each time comparing people, he always slept; when they awoke, then he obtained treachery and deceit; the crowd all feared Zhi's exposing plucking, some thought he had technique; none dared deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Both counties were populous, hugging the capital, and riddled with sharp practice. During hearings Zhi often appeared to doze; the moment a suspect woke to the trap, Zhi had caught the lie. People dreaded his knack for exposure; some swore he used magic— no one dared cheat him.

sentences.zh: 使人投算，祗听其读而心计之，不差升合，其精如此。

translations.literal: He had men cast counting-rods; Zhi listened to their reading and mentally calculated them, not missing a sheng or a ge; his precision was thus.
translations.idiomatic: When clerks called out figures from the counting board, he listened and ran the totals in his head without missing a single measure— such was his precision.

sentences.zh: 汶山夷不安，以祗为汶山太守，民夷服信。

translations.literal: The Wenshan barbarians were not peaceful; with Zhi as Wenshan administrator, the people and barbarians submitted in trust.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wenshan tribes grew restless, Zhi was sent as their prefect; Han and native alike trusted him.

sentences.zh: 迁广汉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 后夷反叛，辞“令得前何府君，乃能安我耳”！

translations.literal: Later the barbarians rebelled, declaring in excuse, "Only if we get the former Prefect He can you pacify us!"
translations.idiomatic: They rose again, insisting, "Bring back the former Prefect He as before or we will not be quiet!"

sentences.zh: 时难屈祗，拔祗族人为，汶山复得安。

translations.literal: At the time Zhi could not conveniently be relieved; they raised a clansman of Zhi's to the post; Wenshan again obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhi could not be moved without trouble, a kinsman of his was promoted to the vacancy and Wenshan calmed down again.

sentences.zh: 转祗为犍为。

translations.literal: They transferred Zhi to Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was then shifted to Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 年四十八卒，如直所言。

translations.literal: At age forty-eight he died, as Zhi had spoken.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-eight, exactly as Zhao Zhi had foretold.

sentences.zh: 后有广汉王离，字伯元，亦以才幹显。

translations.literal: Later there was Wang Li of Guanghan, courtesy name Boyuan, who also became eminent for administrative talent.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Li of Guanghan, courtesy name Boyuan, likewise won renown for his executive ability.

sentences.zh: 为督军从事，推法平当，稍迁，代祗为犍为太守，治有美绩，虽聪明不及祗，而文采过之也。〉

translations.literal: He served as supervising army adjutant, applied the law evenhandedly, rose step by step, replaced Zhi as administrator of Qianwei, and left a fine record in office; though he was not as quick-witted as Zhi, his literary polish surpassed Zhi's.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through supervising army adjutant, earned a reputation for fair adjudication, and eventually succeeded He Zhi as prefect of Qianwei with a distinguished tenure. He lacked Zhi's lightning mind but outshone him in literary grace.

sentences.zh: 費詩字公舉，犍為南安人也。

translations.literal: Fei Shi, courtesy name Gongju, was a man of Nanan in Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Shi, whose courtesy name was Gongju, came from Nanan in Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 劉璋時為綿竹令，先主攻綿竹時，詩先舉城降。

translations.literal: In Liu Zhang's time he was magistrate of Mianzhu; when the First Lord attacked Mianzhu, Shi was the first to raise the city in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Zhang he governed Mianzhu. When the First Lord besieged the town, Shi was first to open the gates and submit.

sentences.zh: 成都既定，先主領益州牧，以詩為督軍從事，出為牂牁太守，還為州前部司馬。

translations.literal: After Chengdu was settled, the First Lord took the title shepherd of Yi Province, appointed Shi supervising army adjutant, sent him out as administrator of Zangke, and recalled him to serve as forward army marshal of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chengdu fell, the First Lord assumed stewardship of Yi Province, named Shi supervising army adjutant, posted him to Zangke, then brought him back as the province's forward army marshal.

sentences.zh: 先主為漢中王，遣詩拜關羽為前將軍，羽聞黃忠為後將軍，

translations.literal: When the First Lord became king of Hanzhong, he sent Shi to invest Guan Yu as forward general; Yu heard that Huang Zhong had been named rear general,
translations.idiomatic: After the First Lord declared himself king of Hanzhong, he dispatched Shi to present Guan Yu with the commission of forward general. When Yu learned that Huang Zhong had been made rear general,

translations.literal: (Yu)
translations.idiomatic: (Guan Yu)

sentences.zh: 怒曰：「大丈夫終不與老兵同列！

translations.literal: angrily said, "A great man in the end will not stand in the same file as an old soldier!"
translations.idiomatic: he fumed, "A true man does not end his career ranked beside some weather-beaten veteran!"

sentences.zh: 」不肯受拜。

translations.literal: He was unwilling to accept the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 詩謂羽曰：「夫立王業者，所用非一。

translations.literal: Shi said to Yu, "To found a king's enterprise, one does not rely on a single kind of man.
translations.idiomatic: Shi told him, "Building an empire takes more than one sort of talent.

sentences.zh: 昔蕭、曹與高祖少小親舊，而陳、韓亡命後主，論其班列，韓最居上，未聞蕭、曹以此為怨。

translations.literal: In antiquity Xiao He and Cao Can were childhood intimates of the High Ancestor, while Chen He and Han Xin were later chiefs who arrived as fugitives; judging their order of rank, Han Xin stood highest— I have never heard that Xiao and Cao resented it for that.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Xiao He and Cao Can grew up with Gaozu, whereas Chen He and Han Xin joined him later as fugitive adventurers; when ranks were fixed, Han Xin stood at the top, yet Xiao and Cao raised no complaint.

sentences.zh: 今

translations.literal: Now
translations.idiomatic: Today

sentences.zh: （漢王）

translations.literal: (King of Han)
translations.idiomatic: (the Prince of Han)

sentences.zh: [漢中王]以一時之功隆崇於漢升，然意之輕重，寧當與君侯齊乎！

translations.literal: [King of Hanzhong] for merit won in a single campaign has honored Hansheng, yet in the weight the ruler attaches to you, could it really be equal to you, lord marquis!
translations.idiomatic: [The king of Hanzhong] has exalted Hansheng for one battle, but in the ruler's heart your place still outweighs his— can you doubt it?

sentences.zh: 且王與君侯臂猶一體，同休等戚，禍福共之，愚為君侯不宜計官號之高下、爵祿之多少為意也。

translations.literal: Moreover the king and you, lord marquis, are like one arm and trunk, sharing ease and peril alike, fortune and misfortune as one— I foolishly think you, lord marquis, ought not to set your mind on the relative height of titles or the more or less of fiefs and stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, you and the king are limb and body, bound in the same fortune; it ill becomes you, my lord, to fuss over who ranks higher or who earns more.

sentences.zh: 僕一介之使，銜命之人，君侯不受拜，如是便還，但相為惜此舉動，恐有後悔耳！

translations.literal: I am a petty envoy, a man bearing a mandate— if you, lord marquis, do not accept the investiture, I shall simply turn back— only I would regret such a gesture on both our parts, for I fear you may later regret it!"
translations.idiomatic: I am only a courier with orders in my sleeve. If you refuse the seal, I must ride home empty-handed— and both of us may rue what pride has cost you!"

sentences.zh: 」羽大感悟，遂即受拜。

translations.literal: Yu was greatly moved to insight, thereupon immediately accepted the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu took the point, accepted the commission, and the crisis passed.

sentences.zh: 後群臣議欲推漢中王稱尊號，詩上疏曰：「殿下以曹操父子逼主篡位，故乃羈旅萬里，糾合士眾，將以討賊。

translations.literal: Later the assembled ministers debated raising the king of Hanzhong to imperial dignity; Shi submitted a memorial saying, "Your highness, because Cao Cao and his son forced the sovereign and usurped the throne, therefore wandered ten thousand li, rallied knights and hosts, intending to punish the traitors.
translations.idiomatic: When the court began to urge the Prince of Hanzhong to take the imperial title, Shi memorialized: "You left home because the Caos coerced the emperor and stole the mandate; you crossed a thousand leagues to gather an army meant to destroy rebels.

sentences.zh: 今天敵未克，而先主自立，恐人心疑惑。

translations.literal: Now Heaven's great enemy is not yet conquered, yet the First Lord first establishes himself— I fear the people's hearts will waver in doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's great foe is still unbeaten, yet you would elevate yourself first— the people will only grow doubtful of your purpose.

sentences.zh: 昔高祖與楚約，先破秦者王。

translations.literal: In antiquity the High Ancestor covenanted with Chu that whoever first defeated Qin would be king.
translations.idiomatic: Remember how Gaozu bargained with Chu that whoever broke Qin first would take the kingship.

sentences.zh: 及屠咸陽，獲子嬰，猶懷推讓，況今殿下未出門庭，便欲自立邪！

translations.literal: When he slaughtered his way into Xianyang and seized Ziying, he still harbored yielding and deference— how much more, when your highness has not yet stepped beyond your gate and courtyard, can you wish to establish yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Even after he stormed Xianyang and held the surrendered emperor, he still hung back from claiming the throne. How can you, who have not yet left your own courtyard, leap ahead to crown yourself?"

sentences.zh: 愚臣誠不為殿下取也。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant truly cannot approve this for your highness.
translations.idiomatic: This is a step your servant cannot in good conscience endorse.

sentences.zh: 」由是忤指，左遷部永昌從事。

translations.literal: From this he ran counter to the intention and was transferred left to serve as adjutant of the Yongchang section.
translations.idiomatic: For that bluntness he was demoted to adjutant for the Yongchang office.

sentences.zh: 〈习凿齿曰：夫创本之君，须大定而后正己，纂统之主，俟速建以系众心，是故惠公朝虏而子圉夕立，更始尚存而光武举号，夫岂忘主徼利，社稷之故也。

translations.literal: Xi Zuochi says: A founder who lays the root must wait for great stability before fixing himself in place; a successor who inherits the line must rely on swift enthronement to bind everyone's heart— therefore Duke Hui was captured at dawn and Ziyu enthroned that same evening; Gengshi still lived yet Guangwu assumed his title— it was not that they forgot their sovereign or grasped for private gain, but the altars of soil and grain compelled it.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi argues that a dynastic founder waits until the realm is settled before claiming supreme style, whereas a restorer must move quickly to steady the people— hence Jin Hui Gong could be taken captive at dawn while his heir Ziyu was enthroned that same night, or Guangwu could raise his banner while Gengshi still sat on the throne. Their haste served the altars of state, not private ambition.

sentences.zh: 今先主纠合义兵，将以讨贼。

translations.literal: Now the First Lord has rallied righteous troops intending to punish the traitor.
translations.idiomatic: Here the First Lord has raised a loyal host to strike the usurper.

sentences.zh: 贼强祸大，主没国丧，二祖之庙，绝而不祀，苟非亲贤，孰能绍此？

translations.literal: The traitor is strong and the calamity great, the ruler has perished and the state is in mourning, the shrines of the two ancestors are cut off and receive no sacrifice— if not for a kinsman and worthy, who could carry this on?
translations.idiomatic: The rebel still towers over us; the Son of Heaven is gone and the dynasty mourns; the twin shrines stand empty. If not for a worthy of the blood, who could renew the line?

sentences.zh: 嗣祖配天，非咸阳之譬，杖正讨逆，何推让之有？

translations.literal: To succeed the ancestor and match Heaven is not the Xianyang precedent; wielding righteousness to chastise rebellion— where is there room for yielding and yielding!
translations.idiomatic: Continuing the ancestral cult is not the same as Gaozus polite pause at Xianyang; you march under the banner of legitimacy— there is no call for false modesty now.

sentences.zh: 於此时也，不知速尊有德以奉大统，使民欣反正，世睹旧物，杖顺者齐心，附逆者同惧，可谓闇惑矣。

translations.literal: At this time, not knowing to hasten to honor the virtuous to uphold the great line, so that the people rejoice in returning to rectification, the age beholds the old tokens restored, those who hold obedience unite their hearts, those who cling to rebellion share fear— this can be called benighted and confused.
translations.idiomatic: Yet instead of enthroning the worthiest man to reunite the mandate, letting the people see the old order restored and the wavering rally while traitors tremble, you hesitate— that is sheer muddle.

sentences.zh: 其黜降也宜哉！

translations.literal: His demotion was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder Fei Shi was cast down!

sentences.zh: 臣松之以为凿齿论议，惟此论最善。〉

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi thinks that among Zuochi's arguments, only this argument is the best.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks that of all Xi Zuochi's opinions, this one alone hits the mark.

sentences.zh: 建興三年，隨諸葛亮南行，歸至漢陽縣，降人李鴻來詣亮，亮見鴻，時蔣琬與詩在坐。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianxing he followed Zhuge Liang south; on the return he reached Hanyang county; the surrendered man Li Hong came to visit Liang; Liang received Hong— at the time Jiang Wan and Shi were seated.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianxing he accompanied Liang on the southern expedition. On the way back they stopped at Hanyang, where the defector Li Hong sought an audience. Liang received him while Jiang Wan and Fei Shi sat in.

sentences.zh: 鴻曰：「聞過孟達許，適見王沖從南來，言往者達之去就，明公切齒，欲誅達妻子，賴先主不聽言。

translations.literal: Hong said, "I passed Meng Da's camp and just saw Wang Chong coming from the south; speaking of how in the past Da went over or stayed, the enlightened duke gnashed his teeth wishing to execute Da's wife and children, relying on the First Lord not listening to the words."
translations.idiomatic: Hong said, "I stopped at Meng Da's camp and met Wang Chong riding north. Chong told how, when Da first changed sides, you gnashed your teeth and meant to execute his family until the First Lord forbade it.

sentences.zh: 達曰：『諸葛亮見顧有本末，終不爾也。

translations.literal: Da said, "Zhuge Liang looks after me with beginning and end; in the end he will not be thus."
translations.idiomatic: Da answered that Zhuge Liang had always treated him fairly and would never go that far.

sentences.zh: 』盡不信沖言，委仰明公，無復已已。

translations.literal: He completely did not trust Chong's words, leans on and looks up to the enlightened duke, without further end."
translations.idiomatic: He put no faith in Chong's story and still places his whole trust in you, my lord— without reserve."

sentences.zh: 」亮謂琬、詩曰：「還都當有書與子度相聞。

translations.literal: Liang said to Wan and Shi, "When we return to the capital there ought to be a letter to Zidu for mutual communication."
translations.idiomatic: Liang told Wan and Shi, "Once we are back in Chengdu I shall write to Zidu to reopen contact."

sentences.zh: 」詩進曰：「孟達小子，昔事振威不忠，後又背叛先主，反覆之人，何足與書邪！

translations.literal: Shi advanced saying, "Meng Da the petty fellow, formerly served Lord Zhenwei without loyalty, later again betrayed the First Lord— a man who turns and turns— what is worthy of writing a letter!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi broke in: "Meng Da is a faithless wretch who betrayed Liu Zhang and then our sovereign. A man like that does not deserve a letter from you!"

sentences.zh: 」亮默然不答。

translations.literal: Liang silently did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Liang said nothing.

sentences.zh: 亮欲誘達以為外援，竟與達書曰：「往年南征，歲

translations.literal: Liang wished to entice Da to be an external aid; in the end he wrote to Da saying, "In former years on the southern campaign, the years end
translations.idiomatic: Still hoping to win Da as an ally beyond the border, Liang finally wrote: "During the last southern expedition the year closed

sentences.zh: （未及）

translations.literal: (not yet reached)
translations.idiomatic: (before I could)

sentences.zh: [末及]還，適與李鴻會於漢陽，承知消息，慨然永歎，以存足下平素之志，豈徒空托名榮，貴為乘離乎！

translations.literal: [end not yet] returned; it happened I met Li Hong in Hanyang— receiving the news I sigh with lasting sorrow, cherishing in my heart your former intent— could it be only empty entrusting of empty fame and glory, valuing being borne apart!"
translations.idiomatic: [before I could] return I met Li Hong at Hanyang. His news moved me deeply, for I know the purpose you once avowed— surely you do not mean to cling to hollow titles while we remain sundered!"

sentences.zh: 嗚呼孟子，斯實劉封侵陵足下，以傷先主待士之義。

translations.literal: Alas Master Meng, this was truly Liu Feng encroaching on you, thereby injuring the First Lord's meaning toward gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, my friend, Liu Feng's bullying of you was what soured the First Lord's faith in treating men generously.

sentences.zh: 又鴻道王沖造作虛語，云足下量度吾心，不受沖說。

translations.literal: Moreover Hong reported Wang Chong fabricated empty words, saying you gauged my mind and did not receive Chong's persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: Hong also said Wang Chong invented rumors, yet you read my heart and refused to believe him.

sentences.zh: 尋表明之言，追平生之好，依依東望，故遣有書。

translations.literal: Following the clear words of the memorial, tracing the friendship of a lifetime, yearning east I gaze; therefore I dispatch this letter.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting the plain words of my earlier memorial and the friendship we once shared, I gaze eastward and send this note.

sentences.zh: 」達得亮書，數相交通，辭欲叛魏。

translations.literal: When Da obtained Liang's letter, repeatedly they exchanged communication; his words wished to rebel against Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Once the letter reached him, he and Liang traded several messages, and he began plotting to revolt from Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏遣司馬宣王征之，即斬滅達。

translations.literal: Wei sent Sima Yi, king of Xuan, to campaign against him; immediately executed and extinguished Da.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Sima Yi against him; Da was caught and killed at once.

sentences.zh: 亮亦以達無款誠之心，故不救助也。

translations.literal: Liang also because Da had no heart of sincere good faith, therefore did not go to his rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Liang never marched to his aid, for he knew Da lacked genuine loyalty.

sentences.zh: 蔣琬秉政，以詩為諫議大夫，卒於家。

translations.literal: Jiang Wan held the government, appointed Shi remonstrance counsellor; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiang Wan's administration Shi was named remonstrance counsellor and ended his days in private life.

sentences.zh: 王沖者，廣漢人也。

translations.literal: Wang Chong was a man of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong came from Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 為牙門將，統屬江州李嚴。

translations.literal: He was camp gate general, under the command of Li Yan of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as camp-gate general under Li Yan, the Jiangzhou commander.

sentences.zh: 為嚴所疾，懼罪降魏。

translations.literal: Yan detested him; fearing punishment he surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yan hated him; dreading a reckoning, Chong fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏以沖為樂陵太守。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Chong administrator of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made him prefect of Leling.

sentences.zh: 〈孙盛蜀世谱曰：诗子立，晋散骑常侍。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng's Shu pedigree says: Shi's son Li became Jin supernumerary palace attendant and cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng's Shu genealogy records that Shi's son Fei Li rose to supernumerary palace attendant and cavalier attendant-in-ordinary under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 自后益州诸费有名位者，多是诗之后也。〉

translations.literal: From afterward the various Fei of Yi Province who had fame and position were mostly Shi's posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the prominent Fei clansmen in Yi Province thereafter traced their line to Shi.

sentences.zh: 评曰：霍峻孤城不倾，王连固节不移，向朗好学不倦，张裔肤敏应机，杨洪乃心忠公，费诗率意而言，皆有可纪焉。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Huo Jun's lone city did not topple; Wang Lian's firm integrity did not shift; Xiang Lang was fond of learning without weariness; Zhang Yi was quick of skin and answered the moment; Yang Hong's heart was loyal to the duke; Fei Shi's words followed his ideas straight out— all have something worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: The historian concludes: Huo Jun held a single citadel unbroken; Wang Lian kept his integrity unbent; Xiang Lang never tired of study; Zhang Yi was alert and resourceful; Yang Hong gave his whole heart to the state; Fei Shi spoke his mind without flattery— each deserves to be remembered.

sentences.zh: 以先主之广济，诸葛之准绳，诗吐直言，犹用陵迟，况庸后乎哉！

translations.literal: With the First Lord's broad succor and Zhuge's plumb line, when Shi spat direct words, still he suffered setback— how much more mediocre successors!
translations.idiomatic: Even under a ruler as magnanimous as the First Lord and a minister as exacting as Zhuge Liang, blunt counsel earned Fei Shi only demotion— what hope, then, for lesser lords who followed?
